title: Add route config helpers for quantization enablement (plus examples)
author: Ibrahim Khan
body:
## Summary
Adds first-class Python SDK helpers for configuring route-level quantization enablement, including canary percentage and "effective" status inspection. This PR is intentionally scoped to Redwood-published Quantization Profile Library workflows (no user-supplied profiles).

This is the Python-side companion to the control plane endpoints introduced in the core service (see redwood PRs: pr_28861_console_api_endpoint_route_quantization_settings.json + pr_28792_route_policy_quantization_enablement_flag.json). The SDK helpers are thin wrappers around the route settings API with validation and ergonomics.

## Motivation
Customers asked to selectively enable quantization only for specific workloads (e.g., background summarization routes) and to safely roll out via canaries. While Console will cover many cases, SDK-level methods are needed for:
- IaC-style route provisioning and config drift detection
- automated rollouts (CI / release jobs)
- quick experimentation / scripts without touching the Console

## What’s included
- `RoutesClient.get_quantization_settings(route_id)` and `RoutesClient.update_quantization_settings(route_id, ...)`
- Typed models:
  - `QuantizationMode` (DISABLED | ENABLED | CANARY)
  - `QuantizationSettings` (requested config)
  - `QuantizationStatus` (effective server-resolved state, including profile id/version when available)
- Client-side validation:
  - canary percentage must be 0..100
  - mutually exclusive fields for `mode` vs explicit booleans
- Backwards compatibility behavior:
  - If the server does not support route quantization settings (404 / feature disabled), raise `FeatureNotAvailableError` with actionable message
  - If the server supports settings but the org lacks permission, surface 403 with existing `PermissionDeniedError`
- Examples:
  - `examples/quantization/enable_canary_on_route.py`
  - `examples/quantization/disable_on_route.py`
  - `examples/quantization/read_effective_status.py`
- Docs: README snippet under "Routes" + short section in "Cost optimization" pointing users to route-level controls

## API shape
This PR aligns with the API conventions doc (route-scoped config, auditable changes, no request-time headers for persistent config). The SDK calls:
- `GET /v1/routes/{route_id}/settings/quantization`
- `PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id}/settings/quantization`

## Example
```py
from redwood import Redwood
from redwood.errors import FeatureNotAvailableError

client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"]) 

try:
    # Ramp to 10% canary on a background summarization route
    client.routes.update_quantization_settings(
        route_id="rt_8f2QmZ...",
        mode="CANARY",
        canary_percent=10,
        reason="enable int8 canary for batch summaries"
    )

    status = client.routes.get_quantization_status(route_id="rt_8f2QmZ...")
    print(status.effective_mode, status.profile_id, status.profile_version)
except FeatureNotAvailableError as e:
    print("Quantization settings not enabled on this deployment:", e)
```

## Notes / limitations
- The SDK does not attempt to choose a specific quantization profile. Profile resolution remains server-side (model + hardware + compatibility matrix + policy).
- We expose `profile_id` and `profile_version` only when the server includes them in the status payload.
- Canary percent is best-effort and subject to server-side gating/rollout policies.

## Test plan
- Unit tests for validation and error mapping
- Contract-style tests with mocked HTTP layer to ensure payloads match backend expectations
- Manual: against staging with quantization settings enabled

## Checklist
- [x] Added types + client methods
- [x] Added examples
- [x] Added docs
- [x] Added tests
- [x] No behavior change to existing route APIs

## Follow-ups
- Add similar helpers to TS SDK (tracked separately)
- Consider a small CLI wrapper in `redwood-tools` for "enable canary" flows used by SRE runbooks
commits: sdk(python): add QuantizationSettings/Status models for routes
sdk(python): implement get/update quantization route settings endpoints
docs/examples: add route-level quantization enablement scripts
tests: validate canary percent and map 404->FeatureNotAvailableError
checks: CI summary: python-lint (ruff) ✅, mypy ✅, unit-tests (py3.10/3.11) ✅, packaging ✅, docs-build ✅
conversation:
Alex Martinez (review): Can we avoid introducing another bool flag + mode enum? It’s easy for users to set conflicting params.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Good call. Pushed an update: `update_quantization_settings()` now takes `mode` as the primary field and `enabled` was removed. We still accept `canary_percent` only when `mode=CANARY`, validated client-side.

Wei Chen (review): Please confirm this uses route config endpoints (persistent) and not per-request headers. Also, error message on 404 should mention feature gating and Private deployments.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Confirmed: this is `PATCH /v1/routes/{id}/settings/quantization` only. Updated `FeatureNotAvailableError` message to include (a) server version, (b) feature flag, and (c) Private/Dedicated deployment rollout caveat.

Dylan Brooks (review): In Console we show “effective” state (after policy/compat checks). Can the SDK expose that too? Customers will script drift checks.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Added `get_quantization_status()` which returns effective mode + profile_id/version when present. Kept `get_quantization_settings()` for the requested config.

Nikhil Sharma (review): Any changes needed for backwards compat with older RoutesClient? Also add an example that disables quantization quickly.
Ibrahim Khan (author): No breaking change: new methods only. Added `disable_on_route.py` example.

Alex Martinez (final): Looks good after refactor + examples. Approved.
Wei Chen (final): Approved.
Dylan Brooks (final): Approved.

Merged via squash after green CI.
